issues.detail: The Vietnamese 'quở trách' (reprimanded/rebuked) is a subjective interpretation. The Greek 'ἐπετιμησεν' means 'commanded' or 'ordered'. While 'rebuked' conveys the authority, 'commanded' is the more accurate translation of the action.

The Vietnamese 'người chờ dậy' (waited to get up) adds a nuance of waiting that is not in the Greek 'δε αναστασα' (without rising/immediately). The Greek implies he didn't even have time to stand up before starting to serve.
